doc.title: Ruth Brisbane interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013

title: Putting together an act: keys, lead sheets, interpretation
summary: Fritz Pollard coached her on endings, song sequence, keys and lead sheets; she knew none of the musicians.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And you said that you went to this person to get an act together.
That’s sort of the responsibility of a singer, right? If you want to work you should have some kind of —

You’re supposed to have an act, which I didn’t realize at the time. An act? You get up and sing you know. But I had it and so forth, and then he would correct me, “No, no, I don’t want that Sarah Vaughan ending, I want a straight ending” or something like that on a song. And I helped pick out songs in sequence.
And did he go through and get your keys for you?
Oh yes. Your keys and he was very good for helping you with interpretation.
And did you carry music with you? Like lead sheets to give to —
They would write up lead sheets, yes, they would, I forgot about that, yes.
Well when you went to this — we are talking a lot about that one gig, but I’m sort of curious, did you know any of the musicians before you got there?

I knew none of the musicians. In fact when you say that, I had a job where Meharry Medical School is, I think it’s Memphis. And a lot of the musicians were from the medical school. Excellent musicians. Yeah. But they were in school, they were in medical school.
